segments.text: I almost died from bad posture, and that's not an exaggeration. A few years ago, a routine MRI showed that I have genetically narrow jugular veins, which meant my bad posture was restricting blood flow from my brain to my heart.

Even with normal veins, poor posture may be doing the same thing to you. These are the four tips I learned from a specialist that changed my life. Imagine there's a string running through your spine pulling you straight up. This is your starting point. Keep [music] screens at eye level. Now, I know this looks ridiculous, but your phone is the worst. Looking down 45° puts 49 lb of load on your cervical spine. With computers, use a monitor or laptop stand. Move every 30 minutes. A quick stretch will help reset your body to have fresh posture. Lastly, strengthen the muscles at the base of your skull. I did two exercises twice a week, one set

to fatigue. After doing these things consistently, my white matter hyperintensities, these are spots indicating potential damage in the brain's white matter, dropped 9 years of biological age in less than 60 days. Friends, posture isn't just cosmetic. It straight-up saved my life.
